## python-roku

Synchronous ECP client built on requests, one of the oldest Roku libraries · [upstream](https://github.com/jcarbaugh/python-roku) · licence BSD-3-Clause · last green `4.1.0`

| Run | Client | Emulator | Runtime | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-07 | 4.1.0 | 1.0.0 | Python 3.13.11 | pass |
| 2026-10-07 | 4.1.0 | 0.2.0 | Python 3.13.11 | pass |

### Latest run, step by step (2026-10-07)

| Step | Action | `roku-streaming-stick-4k-3820eu2` | `tcl-roku-tv-32s357` |
|---|---|---|---|
| device-info and the app list | identify | known gap | ok |
| active app, power state and channels | query-state | — | ok |
| navigation and playback keys | key | — | ok |
| literal text 'tvemu42' | text | — | ok |
| volume up, down and mute | volume | — | ok |
| power off and on | power | — | ok |
| standby reported by device-info | query-state | — | known failure |
| launch an installed application | launch | — | ok |
| open an application's store page | launch | — | ok |
| an application's icon | query-state | — | known gap |
| search for a keyword | search | — | known gap |
| a touch at a point | pointer | — | known gap |
| motion-sensor input | pointer | — | known gap |

### Known gaps

Requests this client sends that no capture answers. The emulator refuses them rather than invent an answer.

- `query/device-info` (only `roku-streaming-stick-4k-3820eu2`): The 12.0.0 stick capture holds no device-info exchange, and the contract answers 501 for it. `device_info` is the first thing this client reads, so on this profile it stops there.
- `POST /search/browse`: `search()` opens the search screen. No capture holds this request or its answer, so the emulator refuses it; recording it off a set closes the gap.
- `query/icon/*`: `icon()` fetches an application's artwork. No capture holds an HTTP icon answer, so the emulator refuses it rather than serve an invented image.
- `POST /input`: `touch()` and the motion-sensor methods post to /input. No capture holds the request or its answer, and the emulator models no pointer or sensors for this television.

### Known failures

Steps the emulator answers, but not as this client expects, for a reason already understood. Each one is still a failure; it is listed so a run can tell it from a new one.

- standby reported by device-info (only `tcl-roku-tv-32s357`): After PowerOff the emulator keeps replaying the captured device-info, whose power-mode is PowerOn, so `power_state` stays On. Only PowerOn is captured; a capture of the set in DisplayOff closes this.

### Known gaps

Requests this client sends that no capture answers. The emulator refuses them rather than invent an answer.

- `query/device-info` (only `roku-streaming-stick-4k-3820eu2`): The 12.0.0 stick capture holds no device-info exchange, and the contract answers 501 for it. `info()` is the first thing this client reads, so on this profile it stops there.
- `POST /search/browse`: `search()` opens the search screen. No capture holds this request or its answer, so the emulator refuses it; recording it off a set closes the gap.
- `query/icon/*`: `icon()` fetches an application's artwork. No capture holds an HTTP icon answer, so the emulator refuses it rather than serve an invented image.

### Known failures

Steps the emulator answers, but not as this client expects, for a reason already understood. Each one is still a failure; it is listed so a run can tell it from a new one.

- standby reported by device-info (only `tcl-roku-tv-32s357`): After PowerOff the emulator keeps replaying the captured device-info, whose power-mode is PowerOn, so `info().powerMode` stays PowerOn. Only PowerOn is captured; a capture of the set in DisplayOff closes this.

## rokuecp

Asynchronous ECP client, the library behind Home Assistant's Roku integration · [upstream](https://github.com/ctalkington/python-rokuecp) · licence MIT · last green `0.19.5`

| Run | Client | Emulator | Runtime | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-07 | 0.19.5 | 1.0.0 | Python 3.13.11 | pass |
| 2026-10-07 | 0.19.5 | 0.2.0 | Python 3.13.11 | pass |

### Latest run, step by step (2026-10-07)

| Step | Action | `roku-streaming-stick-4k-3820eu2` | `tcl-roku-tv-32s357` |
|---|---|---|---|
| device-info, apps and channels | identify | known gap | ok |
| active app, media and channel state | query-state | — | ok |
| navigation and playback keys | key | — | ok |
| literal text 'tvemu42' | text | — | ok |
| volume up, down and mute | volume | — | ok |
| power off and on | power | — | ok |
| standby reported by device-info | query-state | — | known failure |
| launch an application with a deep link | launch | — | ok |
| tune a broadcast channel | launch | — | ok |
| search for a keyword | search | — | known gap |
| play a URL on the device | cast | — | known gap |

### Known gaps

Requests this client sends that no capture answers. The emulator refuses them rather than invent an answer.

- `POST /search/browse`: `search()` and the `search` remote key open the search screen. No capture holds this request or its answer, so the emulator refuses it; recording it off a set closes the gap.
- `POST /input/15985`: `play_on_roku()` hands a URL to the Play on Roku channel. No capture holds it, and the emulator plays no media.
- `query/device-info` (only `roku-streaming-stick-4k-3820eu2`): The 12.0.0 stick capture holds no device-info exchange, and the contract answers 501 for it. rokuecp, and with it Home Assistant, asks for device-info before anything else, so on this profile it stops at its first request.

### Known failures

Steps the emulator answers, but not as this client expects, for a reason already understood. Each one is still a failure; it is listed so a run can tell it from a new one.

- standby reported by device-info (only `tcl-roku-tv-32s357`): After PowerOff the emulator keeps replaying the captured device-info, whose power-mode is PowerOn, so the client never sees standby. Only PowerOn is captured; a capture of the set in DisplayOff closes this.
